science.qualification: Photosphere color from a blackbody at the star's published temperature, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret (2017), A&A 600, A30 computes from PHOENIX model atmospheres for the TESS band at 3,345 K and log g 4.94 (u1 0.157, u2 0.453): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Aug 2006
science.description: Radial component of the star's large-scale magnetic field, fitted with ZDIpy to 15 ESPaDOnS spectra of 5 August 2006 to 12 August 2006 (reduced chi-square 1.05, against 15.4 with no field); mean field 509 G. A reduction made in this project, not a published map. Black line: 60 degrees south, below which the star never faces us.
science.title: ESPaDOnS · magnetic map made here · Aug 2006

science.label: Sector 56
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 1.08 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 56 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 3.3%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.76%, the light's own noise being 0.26%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 1.08 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.65, a width of 0.47 and a fit of 1.00, and in all 2 of the star's sectors together a period of 1.08 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.57, a width of 0.48 and a fit of 1.00; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 60°. Gaia DR3 lists 8 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 21% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 56

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffc382, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 83 (September 2024): the map's scale, 96% to 104% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 6.9% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · September 2024
